sections.title: A bounded implementation milestone
sections.markdown: Scheduled60 minutes: brief/prediction10, implementation25, tests15, evidence10. Setup is separate. This milestone implements a durable job queue with a local result ledger. It is designed to expose the hardest small failure: worker A pauses beyond its lease, worker B claims the job, and A later attempts completion. A claim is not a permanent ownership right. Completion must verify current state, token and expiry within the same transaction that commits the local effect.

sections.title: Mechanism and correctness boundary
sections.markdown:
Use jobs(id,payload,state,attempts,available,lease_until,token,last_error) and effects(job_id,result). Enqueue is idempotent for one ID plus identical payload; a different payload under the same ID conflicts. Claim begins an immediate transaction, recovers expired running leases to an eligible state, selects one available job, increments attempts and mints a fresh token before commit.

Complete begins a transaction, checks that the job is running with the supplied current unexpired token, inserts the unique local effect and marks done, then commits. This makes the local ledger and job state one atomic boundary. It does not make an external email, payment call or filesystem change atomic with SQLite. Name that limitation every time you explain the result; a distributed system is not exactly-once merely because one table has a unique key.

The acceptance history claims a ten-second lease at the fake current time, advances exactly ten seconds, and claims again. The token must change. Completion using the old token raises PermissionError and applies nothing; completion using the new token records one effect and done state. Real wall-clock sleeps are unnecessary for this deterministic boundary test.

sections.title: Use the prepared learner skeleton
sections.markdown:
Read projects/P3.md and projects/README.md. Edit projects/learner/jobs.py; the TODOs identify this milestone. Run the focused acceptance test from the repository root:

~~~powershell
$env:ACADEMY_LAB_IMPLEMENTATION = 'learner'
py -3 -m unittest discover -s projects/tests -p test_projects.py -k P3_1 -v
Remove-Item Env:ACADEMY_LAB_IMPLEMENTATION
~~~

The default test implementation is the completed reference; setting the variable selects your learner code. A learner TODO failure is intentional, not missing teaching. If your launcher is python or python3, substitute it for py -3. The baseline uses only the Python standard library and temporary test databases. No app endpoint executes your code.

Worker A pauses beyond expiry while B reclaims. A resumes and attempts a stale commit. Checking only job ID would allow it; validate token, state and current lease within the commit transaction.

Stop when the focused test passes and you have recorded the stated evidence. Do not spend the hour constructing a new server framework or extending unrelated features.

sections.title: Record what the test actually shows
sections.markdown:
Demonstrate stale-worker rejection, current-worker success, and one durable local effect.

Save the exact command, expected result, actual result, fault injected and the final invariant in the Project workspace. Note any untested assumption. The reference implementation and test have been executed; your own implementation needs its own run evidence. Compare with the explicit reference only after attempting the bounded task.

Local workers share one SQLite database. The effect ledger proves only effects stored in the same transaction. An email or payment API outside this database is not exactly-once by this mechanism.

Optional additional practice belongs in a separate session: Add an outbox and idempotent HTTP receiver to demonstrate cross-boundary effect handling.

steps: Implement enqueue, claim and complete. Freeze time, claim a job, advance beyond its lease, and claim again. The second worker receives a different token. Reject completion from the first worker even though it once legitimately owned the job.

exercise.prompt: Implement enqueue, claim and complete. Freeze time, claim a job, advance beyond its lease, and claim again. The second worker receives a different token. Reject completion from the first worker even though it once legitimately owned the job.
rubric: Only the current unexpired claim token may commit a result. The local effect ledger and done state commit atomically; external side effects need their own idempotency boundary.
Demonstrate stale-worker rejection, current-worker success, and one durable local effect.
Reports the implemented guarantee and its limits.
exercise.solution: Persist the job before claiming. Perform expired-lease recovery and selection inside one write transaction so competing workers cannot both obtain the same current claim. Assign a fresh token to each successful claim and retain the deadline. On complete, atomically check state=running, matching token and lease_until > now; otherwise reject before any protected effect. Insert a result keyed by job ID and mark done within the same SQLite transaction. The test must preserve the new worker's result after an old token attempts completion. This establishes a local transactional effect boundary only: an external provider needs its own idempotency or coordination mechanism, addressed in later projects and lessons.
